userStories.title: Allow raw sandbox fallback and expose native sandbox state
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Permit explicit unavailable-sandbox fallback for full/review raw native sessions and report their resolved sandbox state.

**Motivation** — The interactive host's "full" mode is `profile: "full"` with `bashApproval: "raw"` and must keep working on a machine without `srt`, by the user's ruling of 2026-10-24.

**Approach** — **Sandbox floor (US-001).** `nativeProfileRules` accepts `allowUnsandboxed: true` with `bashApproval: "raw"` as well as `"gated"` (still refused with `"escalate"`, and the `ask` profile still forces `gated`). `resolveSessionLauncher` returns no launcher for an unavailable sandbox whenever `allowUnsandboxed` is true, regardless of `raw` vs `gated`, and returns the resolved `SandboxState` beside the launcher. With no launcher the Bash tool already takes its direct-spawn branch (`src/tools/bash.ts`, `opts.launcher` absent) and `rawRefusalFor(undefined)` is `undefined`, so `raw` runs unwrapped with no further change. `openNative` records the state on `BackendInfo.sandbox`, and the facade's `backend` getter in `agent-session.ts`, which today rebuilds the info from `kind` and `capabilities` only, copies `sandbox` through (shallow-frozen).

`nativeProfileRules(profile, raw)` — Target: throws `allowUnsandboxed requires bashApproval "gated" or "raw"` only when `bashApproval === "escalate"`; accepts `allowUnsandboxed: true` with `"raw"` for profiles `full` and `review` (the `ask` profile still throws `profile "ask" requires bashApproval "gated"` first); returns `{ bashApproval, allowUnsandboxed, allowUnsandboxedCommands }` where `allowUnsandboxedCommands` is `raw.allowUnsandboxedCommands === true`; throws `allowUnsandboxedCommands applies to profiles "ask", "full" and "review" only` for `none`/`read` when the field is set.

`resolveSessionLauncher(args)` — Target: `Promise<{ launcher: CommandLauncher | undefined; sandbox: SandboxState }>`. Returns `launcher: undefined` for a non-available launcher whenever `args.allowUnsandboxed` is true; `sandbox` is the launcher's `state` when available, the launcher's `unavailable` state when it was dropped, and `{ kind: "disabled" }` for the `none`/`read` profiles. The error message ends `Pass allowUnsandboxed: true to run without one.`

`BackendInfo` — Target: `{ kind; capabilities; sandbox?: SandboxState }`; `openNative` sets it for the native backend; the ACP backend leaves it absent. `get backend()` — Target: additionally copies `sandbox` (shallow-frozen) when present on `opened.info`.

**Scope** — In: native option validation/profile resolution, launcher-result migration, native info and facade copying; update native-backend-options.test.ts two-field equalities and obsolete raw rejection, session-tool-support.test.ts bare-launcher assertions, and native-backend.test.ts opened.info equality. Out: US-002 request-level unwrapping, US-003 option forwarding/tool advertisement, US-004 approval fields and US-005/006 runtime routing. `SandboxState` is reported once at open; a sandbox that becomes unavailable mid-session is not re-probed. The ACP server (`packages/nax-agent-acp`) does not expose `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxed` with `raw`, `BackendInfo.sandbox` or the `unsandboxed` approval field; its config and translate layers are unchanged.

**Interface** — `readonly allowUnsandboxedCommands?: boolean`, validated as optional boolean. Resolved result: `{ bashApproval, allowUnsandboxed, allowUnsandboxedCommands }`. `resolveSessionLauncher(args)`: `Promise<{ launcher: CommandLauncher | undefined; sandbox: SandboxState }>`. `BackendInfo`: `{ kind; capabilities; sandbox?: SandboxState }`. Mirror the existing allowUnsandboxed schema/rules pattern; do not add export names or change default gated session behavior. Use scripted-session helpers and sandbox deps stubs for session assertions, including the existing direct-spawn fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] nativeProfileRules("full", { model, bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true }) returns { bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false }.
[unit] nativeProfileRules("review", { model, bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true }) returns allowUnsandboxed: true.

[unit] nativeProfileRules("full", { model, bashApproval: "escalate", allowUnsandboxed: true }) throws AgentSessionError with code AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS and message containing 'allowUnsandboxed requires bashApproval "gated" or "raw"'.
[unit] nativeProfileRules("ask", { model, bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true }) throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with message containing 'profile "ask" requires bashApproval "gated"'.
[unit] nativeProfileRules("full", { model, allowUnsandboxedCommands: true }) returns allowUnsandboxedCommands: true.

[unit] nativeProfileRules("read", { model, allowUnsandboxedCommands: true }) throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with message containing 'allowUnsandboxedCommands applies to profiles "ask", "full" and "review" only'.

[unit] nativeProfileRules(profile, { model, allowUnsandboxedCommands }) throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with message containing 'allowUnsandboxedCommands applies to profiles "ask", "full" and "review" only' for either none or read when allowUnsandboxedCommands is set to true or false.
[unit] parseNativeBackendOptions({ model: "p/m", allowUnsandboxedCommands: "yes" }) throws AGENT_SESSION_INVALID_OPTIONS with path context backend.allowUnsandboxedCommands.

[unit] With _sessionSandboxDeps reporting unavailable with reason "srt missing", resolveSessionLauncher({ profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true, root, protectedPaths }) resolves to { launcher: undefined, sandbox: { kind: "unavailable", backend: "srt", reason: "srt missing" } }.

[unit] Under that unavailable probe, resolveSessionLauncher({ profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: false, root, protectedPaths }) rejects with AgentSessionError code AGENT_SESSION_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE whose message ends 'Pass allowUnsandboxed: true to run without one.'.
[unit] With the probe available, resolveSessionLauncher({ profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true, root, protectedPaths }) resolves to a defined launcher.
[unit] With the probe available, resolveSessionLauncher({ profile: "full", bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true, root, protectedPaths }) resolves to a sandbox whose kind is "available".

[unit] resolveSessionLauncher({ profile: "read", bashApproval: "gated", allowUnsandboxed: false, root, protectedPaths }) resolves to { launcher: undefined, sandbox: { kind: "disabled" } } without calling the probe.

[integration] createAgentSession with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxed: true }), profile "full" and an unavailable probe with reason "srt missing" opens with session.backend.sandbox deep-equal to { kind: "unavailable", backend: "srt", reason: "srt missing" }.

[integration] In that raw fallback session, a scripted Bash call { command: "ls" } invokes _bashToolDeps.runArgv with argv [shell, "-c", "ls"], preserving the existing direct-spawn branch when no launcher is present.
[integration] createAgentSession with profile "read" returns session.backend.sandbox deep-equal to { kind: "disabled" }.
[integration] createAgentSession with profile "read" returns session.backend.kind equal to "native".
[integration] createAgentSession with profile "read" returns session.backend.capabilities deep-equal to {}.

[integration] createAgentSession with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "raw" }), profile "full" and an unavailable sandbox rejects with AGENT_SESSION_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE when allowUnsandboxed is absent, preserving the existing failure with the new fallback message.

routing.reasoning: Five source modules migrate an internal return shape and add optional public data using existing option/facade patterns; sandbox and session access boundaries require strict isolated TDD. Standard multi-file integration fits the balanced native profile.

suggestedCriteria: When session.backend exposes a sandbox object, Object.isFrozen(session.backend.sandbox) returns true.
When an opened backend supplies no sandbox field, session.backend has no sandbox key.

modifiedFiles.reason: five `toEqual({ bashApproval, allowUnsandboxed })` assertions ("full defaults to gated", the `ask` default, "read and none accept neither knob", "full accepts…", the review test) pin the two-field result; the invariant is the three-field result with `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false` by default. The assertion that `raw` + `allowUnsandboxed: true` throws `allowUnsandboxed requires bashApproval "gated"` pins the old rule; the invariant is that it resolves and only `escalate` + `allowUnsandboxed` throws.

`toBeUndefined()` on `resolveSessionLauncher`'s result and `launcher?.state.kind` reads pin the bare-launcher return; the invariant is the `{ launcher, sandbox }` result. Hosts the new `resolveSessionLauncher` ACs.

line 79 `expect(opened.info).toEqual({ kind: "native", capabilities: {} })` pins the two-field info and fails once a `read` session reports `sandbox: { kind: "disabled" }`; the invariant is `kind` and `capabilities` unchanged plus the `sandbox` field. Hosts the US-001 session-level ACs.

userStories.title: Run a single launcher request unwrapped
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let a caller explicitly launch one command outside the sandbox without changing launcher state.

**Motivation** — The user's rule: "unreachable" (network, Docker socket, local DB port, device) is handled per command, and the sandbox is never turned off for the session.

**Approach** — **Launcher (US-002).** `LaunchRequest` gains `unwrapped?: true`. `CommandLauncher.run` routes such a request to `runUnwrapped` even when `state.kind === "available"`, with `SandboxRecord { backend: "none", wrapped: false, reason: "requested" }`; `policyFor` and `afterWrapped` are not called for it. The session temp-directory overlay (`TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`) still applies, as for every unwrapped run.

`CommandLauncher.run` — Target: when `req.unwrapped === true`, runs through `runUnwrapped` with `SandboxRecord { backend: "none", wrapped: false, reason: "requested" }`, skipping `policyFor` and `afterWrapped`; every other request is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: optional LaunchRequest member, explicit early runUnwrapped branch in createCommandLauncher, launcher regression tests. Apply the branch after existing temp-directory preparation so overlays and logical argv are preserved, and before state-specific branches so disabled/unavailable requested runs also record requested. Mirror existing disabled unwrapped spawning and available wrapper tests in test/unit/sandbox/launcher.test.ts; stub _launcherDeps.runArgv. Retain its existing wrap-failure regression: an ordinary available request whose backend.wrap throws rejects with SANDBOX_WRAP_FAILED and spawns nothing; explicit request-level escape never turns into automatic fallback. Out: session fallback/state reporting (US-001), model argument/schema/option plumbing (US-003/008), and approval/policy routing (US-004/005/006). Do not add a new spawn API, automatic wrap-failure fallback, session-state mutation or per-call recomputation of launcher-level policy relaxations.

**Interface** — `LaunchRequest`: `readonly unwrapped?: true`. `CommandLauncher.run` accepts the extended request through its existing signature. Result sandbox record: `{ backend: "none", wrapped: false, reason: "requested" }`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createCommandLauncher({ state: available, backend }) running { spec: { kind: "shell", shell, command }, ..., unwrapped: true } calls _launcherDeps.runArgv with argv [shell, "-c", command].
[unit] An available launcher's unwrapped: true run never calls backend.wrap.
[unit] An unwrapped: true run returns sandbox deep-equal to { backend: "none", wrapped: false, reason: "requested" }.
[unit] An unwrapped: true shell run returns executed equal to [shell, "-c", command].
[unit] With afterWrapped and policyFor supplied, an unwrapped: true run invokes neither callback.
[unit] With afterWrapped and policyFor supplied, the same request without unwrapped invokes both callbacks.
[unit] With tmpDir supplied, an unwrapped: true run passes runArgv an env whose TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP all equal that directory.
[unit] A launcher whose state is unavailable returns a sandbox record with wrapped: false and reason: "requested" when run receives unwrapped: true.
[unit] A launcher whose state is disabled returns a sandbox record with wrapped: false and reason: "requested" when run receives unwrapped: true.
[unit] An available launcher calls backend.wrap for a request without unwrapped.
[unit] An available launcher returns wrapped: true for a request without unwrapped.

[unit] When backend.wrap throws for an available launcher's request without unwrapped, launcher.run rejects with NaxError code SANDBOX_WRAP_FAILED, preserving the existing fail-closed behavior rather than falling back to an unwrapped run.
[unit] When backend.wrap throws for a request without unwrapped, _launcherDeps.runArgv is not invoked, preserving the existing no-spawn-on-wrap-failure behavior.

routing.reasoning: One launcher branch plus an additive request field mirrors existing runUnwrapped behavior across two modules; the small, explicit change fits native-luna, with strict TDD for the sandbox escape boundary.

modifiedFiles.reason: hosts the new `unwrapped` ACs; any assertion that an `available` launcher calls `backend.wrap` for every request becomes "for every request without `unwrapped`".

userStories.title: Advertise and forward Bash unsandboxed requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Thread the opt-in to Bash and forward exact-true unsandboxed calls as one unwrapped launcher request.

**Motivation** — The only unsandboxed option is the session-wide `allowUnsandboxed`, which is exactly the "turn the sandbox off for the session because one command needed Docker" outcome the user forbade.

**Approach** — Thread `unsandboxedCommands` from `nativeProfileRules` through `openNative`, `buildSessionToolSupport`, `buildCodingToolSupport` and `buildDeclaredCommandTools` to `createBashTool`, via small extracted helpers so the two baselined functions do not grow in complexity.

Bash `scope` always declares `unsandboxedField: "unsandboxed"`; when the option is on, `inputSchema` gains `unsandboxed` and `unsandboxedReason` and the description gains one appended sentence; when off, schema and description are byte-identical to today.

Bash `run` passes `unwrapped: true` on the launcher request when `input.unsandboxed === true`; with no launcher it direct-spawns.

`BashToolOptions` / `createBashTool` — Target: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`. `scope` always has `unsandboxedField: "unsandboxed"`. When the option is true: `inputSchema` gains `unsandboxed: { type: "boolean" }` and `unsandboxedReason: { type: "string" }`, and the description gains, appended after today's last sentence, `Set "unsandboxed": true with an "unsandboxedReason" only when the command needs the network, a local socket or a device the sandbox blocks.` When false or absent, `inputSchema` and `description` are byte-identical to today's. `run` passes `unwrapped: true` on the launcher request when `input.unsandboxed === true`; with no launcher it direct-spawns as today. The tool itself never checks the option.

`SessionToolSupportArgs` / `buildSessionToolSupport` — Target: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean` (optional, default false), forwarded to `buildCodingToolSupport` as `unsandboxedCommands`. `openNative` destructures `allowUnsandboxedCommands` from `nativeProfileRules` and passes `unsandboxedCommands` to `buildSessionToolSupport`.

`buildDeclaredCommandTools` and `buildCodingToolSupport` receive the flag through one small extracted helper each (for example `unsandboxedToolOptions(args)`), so their complexity does not rise; `callTool`'s single call keeps it under 20.

**Scope** — In: ToolScope metadata, Bash option/schema/text/request changes, and session-to-support-to-Bash propagation. Extend bash.test.ts, bash-sandbox.test.ts, coding-tool-support.test.ts, session-tool-support.test.ts and native-backend.test.ts. Mirror the existing disabled-launcher byte-identical description test; preserve today's default schema keys, required command, interception, env, timeout, abort and audit behavior, including rejection of an empty command before any launch even when the escape flag is true. Out: runtime enablement enforcement and allow-to-ask conversion (US-005/006), approval rendering (US-004), session scenario proof (US-007), and RunCommand exec plumbing (US-008). RunCommand and Exec are not declared for any session profile in this feature; `declaredToolsFor` is unchanged, so an interactive session does not see RunCommand until a later feature declares it. The RunCommand `unsandboxed` argument is exercised at the tool and support level here.

**Interface** — `ToolScope`: `readonly unsandboxedField?: string`. `BashToolOptions`: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`. `SessionToolSupportArgs`, `buildCodingToolSupport` args and `buildDeclaredCommandTools` args: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`. Use US-002's `LaunchRequest.unwrapped` only for exact true and omit the key otherwise. Runtime option creation belongs to US-005; preserve that inter-story boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] createBashTool(opts) with unsandboxedCommands absent produces inputSchema property keys exactly command, timeoutMs, description.
[unit] createBashTool(opts) with unsandboxedCommands absent produces a description equal to the description with unsandboxedCommands: false.
[unit] createBashTool(opts).scope.unsandboxedField equals "unsandboxed" whether or not unsandboxedCommands is set, with scope.commandField still equal to "command".
[unit] createBashTool({ ...opts, unsandboxedCommands: true }).inputSchema.properties declares unsandboxed.type as "boolean" and unsandboxedReason.type as "string".
[unit] createBashTool({ ...opts, unsandboxedCommands: true }).inputSchema.required deep-equals ["command"].

[unit] createBashTool({ ...opts, unsandboxedCommands: true }).description ends with 'Set "unsandboxed": true with an "unsandboxedReason" only when the command needs the network, a local socket or a device the sandbox blocks.'.

[unit] createBashTool({ launcher, unsandboxedCommands: true }).run({ command: "curl x", unsandboxed: true, unsandboxedReason: "needs network" }, ctx) calls launcher.run with unwrapped: true and spec deep-equal to { kind: "shell", shell, command: "curl x" }.
[unit] createBashTool({ launcher, unsandboxedCommands: true }).run({ command: "ls" }, ctx) calls launcher.run with no unwrapped key.
[unit] createBashTool({ launcher, unsandboxedCommands: true }).run({ command: "ls", unsandboxed: "true" }, ctx) calls launcher.run with no unwrapped key.
[unit] createBashTool({ unsandboxedCommands: true }).run({ command: "ls", unsandboxed: true }, ctx) without a launcher calls _bashToolDeps.runArgv with argv [shell, "-c", "ls"].
[unit] That no-launcher Bash run returns a result whose isError is not true.

[unit] buildCodingToolSupport({ ...args, declared: [..., "Bash"], unsandboxedCommands: true }) yields a Bash tool with an unsandboxed inputSchema.properties key; with unsandboxedCommands absent that key is absent.
[unit] buildDeclaredCommandTools({ ...args, unsandboxedCommands: true }) yields a Bash tool with an unsandboxed inputSchema.properties key.

[unit] buildSessionToolSupport({ ...args, unsandboxedCommands: true }) returns a support.tools Bash entry whose inputSchema.properties has unsandboxed; buildSessionToolSupport(args) without the field returns one without that key.

[integration] createAgentSession with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "gated", allowUnsandboxedCommands: true }) and profile "full" advertises a Bash tool whose inputSchema.properties has unsandboxed; the same session without allowUnsandboxedCommands advertises one without that key.

[unit] createBashTool({ launcher, unsandboxedCommands: true }).run({ command: "", unsandboxed: true }, ctx) returns { content: '"command" must be a non-empty string', isError: true }, preserving the existing invalid-command refusal.
[unit] When Bash receives an empty command with unsandboxed: true, neither launcher.run nor _bashToolDeps.runArgv is invoked.

routing.reasoning: Existing launcher and allowUnsandboxed plumbing provide the pattern for additive option forwarding, schema/text extensions and one Bash request flag; no new subsystem is needed. Native-deepseek fits the multi-file wiring, while the session/sandbox security override requires strict isolated TDD.

the `scope.commandField` check at line 180 stays; hosts the `scope.unsandboxedField` AC and the launcher-request `unwrapped` ACs.
the `args()` helper builds `SessionToolSupportArgs`; `unsandboxedCommands` is optional so the helper compiles unchanged; hosts the `buildSessionToolSupport` forwarding AC.
hosts the US-003 session-level advertisement AC.

userStories.title: Carry safe unsandboxed metadata through approvals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose an optional unsandboxed approval flag and a masked bounded explanation through the existing session approval path.

**Motivation** — The user's rule: "unreachable" (network, Docker socket, local DB port, device) is handled per command, and the sandbox is never turned off for the session.

**Approach** — Add `unsandboxed?: true` to `AskRequest`, `ApprovalRequest`, `ApprovalAsk` and the `approval_requested` event body; `createSessionAskLink` and `askPerson` forward it.

New `unsandboxedReasonSuffix(input)` in `ask-request.ts` (masked, capped, with the `no reason given` and `reason withheld` fallbacks).

`resolveAskOutcome` gains the optional `unsandboxed?: { suffix }` argument that sets the flag and appends the suffix to `reason`, leaving `matchedRule` unset when the verdict's `rule` is the synthetic `Unsandboxed(<identity>)`.

`unsandboxedReasonSuffix(input)` — Target: returns ` -- runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: ` + rendered reason, where the rendered reason is `input.unsandboxedReason` passed through `maskForPrompt` and cut to `MAX_ASK_SUMMARY_CHARS` when it is a string; `reason withheld` when masking reports unshowable; `no reason given` when absent or not a string.

`resolveAskOutcome(args)` — Target: new optional `unsandboxed?: { readonly suffix: string }`; when present the built `AskRequest` has `unsandboxed: true` and `reason` = the verdict reason + `suffix`; `matchedRule` is set only when `verdict.rule` came from a real ask rule (the converted-allow verdict passes `rule: "Unsandboxed(<identity>)"` and `matchedRule` stays unset).

Why the approval carries the flag rather than a new ask kind: the session ask path is `approval_requested` -> `session.answer()` (`src/session/session-ask-link.ts`, `src/session/session-ask-port.ts`). One optional field on `AskRequest`, `ApprovalRequest` (which `createSessionAskLink` builds), `ApprovalAsk` (which `createSessionAskPort` derives from it) and the `approval_requested` body reuses that path unchanged for hosts that ignore it.

The reason renderer is `unsandboxedReasonSuffix(input)` in `src/tools/ask-request.ts`, exported from that module (tests import `#src/tools/ask-request`; it is not added to the package's `.` entry). Mask the full reason before cutting, as askSummary already does; do not turn an unsafe reason into an unshowable command or deny the request solely because its reason was withheld. Preserve existing secret-command refusals and cancellation checks.

**Scope** — In: optional approval members, safe reason rendering, AskRequest construction and session link/event forwarding; extend ask-request.test.ts and session-ask-link.test.ts, including direct resolveAskOutcome assertions. Out: detecting/authorizing an unsandboxed request or converting runtime verdicts (US-005/006), launcher changes (US-002), and session end-to-end scenarios (US-007). `AskDecidedBy` gains no new value, and no approval event is emitted under `raw`. The guard-denial ask path (`commandShadow.guard` in `callTool`) does not carry the `unsandboxed` flag; sessions configure no command shadow, so it is inert here. The ACP server (`packages/nax-agent-acp`) does not expose `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxed` with `raw`, `BackendInfo.sandbox` or the `unsandboxed` approval field; its config and translate layers are unchanged. Remembered-approval keys in `packages/nax` do not include the `unsandboxed` flag; whether a remembered plain approval should cover an unsandboxed variant is a later decision.

**Interface** — `AskRequest`, `ApprovalRequest`, `ApprovalAsk` and `approval_requested` body: `readonly unsandboxed?: true`. `resolveAskOutcome` args: `unsandboxed?: { readonly suffix: string }`. Deep-module export: `unsandboxedReasonSuffix(input)`. `createSessionAskLink` copies the field onto ApprovalRequest, createSessionAskPort's rest-spread preserves it, and askPerson conditionally emits it; absent fields remain absent keys.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] unsandboxedReasonSuffix({ unsandboxedReason: "needs network" }) returns ' -- runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: needs network'.
[unit] unsandboxedReasonSuffix({ unsandboxedReason: 42 }) and unsandboxedReasonSuffix({}) each return ' -- runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: no reason given'.
[unit] unsandboxedReasonSuffix({ unsandboxedReason: a 300-character string }) returns a suffix whose rendered reason is exactly 200 characters long.
[unit] unsandboxedReasonSuffix({ unsandboxedReason: a string maskForPrompt reports unshowable }) returns ' -- runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: reason withheld'.

[unit] resolveAskOutcome with an ask verdict whose rule is "Bash(*)" and unsandboxed: { suffix: " -- S" } hands askResolver.resolve an AskRequest with unsandboxed: true, matchedRule: "Bash(*)" and reason equal to the verdict reason followed by ' -- S'.

[unit] resolveAskOutcome with rule "Unsandboxed(Bash)", reason "unsandboxed run requested" and unsandboxed: { suffix: " -- S" } hands askResolver.resolve an AskRequest with rule "Unsandboxed(Bash)", no matchedRule key and reason 'unsandboxed run requested -- S'.
[unit] resolveAskOutcome without unsandboxed hands askResolver.resolve an AskRequest with no unsandboxed key and reason equal to the verdict reason.
[unit] createSessionAskLink(deps).resolve(req) copies unsandboxed: true from AskRequest to deps.port.requestApproval; without the field the forwarded object has no unsandboxed key.
[unit] askPerson(deps, { tool: "Bash", summary, reason, unsandboxed: true }, signal) emits approval_requested with unsandboxed: true; without the field the emitted event has no unsandboxed key.

routing.reasoning: Optional-field forwarding follows the existing approval chain; the only bounded logic is a renderer mirroring askSummary and exclusion of synthetic matchedRule origin. This is standard additive integration for native-deepseek, with strict TDD retained for secret masking and approval metadata.

suggestedCriteria: When unsandboxedReason contains a maskable secret, unsandboxedReasonSuffix returns a masked reason without the original secret text.

modifiedFiles.reason: hosts the `unsandboxedReasonSuffix` ACs; existing imports (`askDenyReason`, `askSummary`, `MAX_ASK_SUMMARY_CHARS`) are unchanged.
hosts the forwarding ACs; any deep-equal on the emitted `approval_requested` body must allow `unsandboxed`.

userStories.title: Enforce unsandboxed enablement before policy evaluation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse disabled escape requests before policy/ask/spawn while retaining ordinary calls, declared-command routing and policy denials.

**Motivation** — There is no per-command escape.

**Approach** — `createCodingToolRuntime` gains `unsandboxed: { enabled, bashApproval }`, set by `buildCodingToolSupport` from `unsandboxedCommands` and the resolved `bashApproval`.

New `resolveUnsandboxedCall` in `runtime-calltool.ts`, called once from `callTool` before `policy.check`, only for identities `Bash` and `Exec`: when not enabled it returns the `{ kind: "error", ... }` refusal (logged through `logCall`); a deny verdict is unchanged; a call without the flag is unchanged; a `RunCommand`-identity call is untouched.

A human deny on an unsandboxed ask returns the `denied` outcome without running the tool.

`resolveUnsandboxedCall(args)` — Target: called by `callTool` once per call, before `opts.policy.check`, with the tool, input, policy identity and the runtime's `unsandboxed` option. Returns `undefined` when the identity is not `Bash` or `Exec`, the scope has no `unsandboxedField`, or `input[field] !== true`. Returns `{ kind: "error", content: "unsandboxed commands are not enabled for this session (allowUnsandboxedCommands)" }` when the option is not enabled.

The unsandboxed routing is one exported helper in `src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts` (330 lines today), `resolveUnsandboxedCall`, which `callTool` in `src/tools/runtime.ts` (569 lines today) calls in one line.

`buildCodingToolSupport` args — Target: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`, forwarded through a small helper to `buildDeclaredCommandTools` and to `createCodingToolRuntime` as `unsandboxed: { enabled, bashApproval: <the locally resolved bashApproval> }`.

For enabled requests return a marker for the later routing work, compute policy exactly as without the flag and preserve the original input for tool execution. Denials must still pass through existing denial rendering without losing breach or changing their reason; no tool runs on denial. Place the early refusal so it records outcome error through logCall semantics before policy.check, even though today's logCall closure is declared after policy evaluation/shadow setup. Keep the helper deep-module-only, avoid adding exports to . or ./internal, and preserve the existing shadow/guard path. userStories.title: Prove session-level unsandboxed Bash behavior
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prove the assembled native session exposes and executes per-command Bash escapes with the specified approval behavior.

**Motivation** — The user's rule: "unreachable" (network, Docker socket, local DB port, device) is handled per command, and the sandbox is never turned off for the session.

**Approach** — No new production code: this story proves the wiring end to end through `createAgentSession` with a scripted model, for `gated` (ask, allow, deny, sandbox stays on), `raw` (no ask), and option off (refusal).

For session-level tests that drive a scripted model and answer asks, mirror `test/unit/session/agent-session-asks.test.ts` (helpers in `test/helpers/agent-session.ts` and `stubSessionSandboxDeps`).

US-006 -> US-007: US-007 asserts a `createAgentSession` whose model requests an unsandboxed Bash call under `gated` yields an `approval_requested` with `unsandboxed: true`, and on allow the stubbed `runArgv` runs the logical argv without `backend.wrap`.

**Scope** — In: extend test/unit/session/native-backend.test.ts with real facade/native/runtime wiring driven by installScriptedProvider, toolRound/textRound and event reader/session.answer. Probe is stubbed available, backend.wrap is observed, and _launcherDeps.runArgv is stubbed so curl x is never executed. Prove allow, deny, later ordinary wrapping, raw no-ask, and disabled-option model error. Restore dependency seams, provider state and sessions with the existing helper lifecycle. This is the explicit binding-spec exception to the generic prohibition on test-only stories, and its deliverable is executable test-code changes. Out: new production behavior already owned by US-001 through US-006; RunCommand support-level work in US-008; new durable audit storage or an approval cache. No tool-audit directory is plumbed into sessions; `buildSessionToolSupport` keeps the non-recording sink, so an unsandboxed run under `raw` leaves no durable session ledger row. Callers that pass `auditDir` to `buildCodingToolSupport` get the `reason: "requested"` record.

**Interface** — Existing test-facing session path: `createAgentSession`, `nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "gated", allowUnsandboxedCommands: true })`, `profile: "full"`, and `session.answer(requestId, { decision: "allow" })` / `session.answer(requestId, { decision: "deny" })`. Model request: `{ command: "curl x", unsandboxed: true, unsandboxedReason: "needs network" }`. Event: `approval_requested` with `unsandboxed: true`. No new production signatures or exports.
acceptanceCriteria: [integration] A full session created with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "gated", allowUnsandboxedCommands: true }), probe available, and a scripted Bash call { command: "curl x", unsandboxed: true, unsandboxedReason: "needs network" } yields approval_requested with tool: "Bash", unsandboxed: true and reason containing 'runs OUTSIDE the sandbox: needs network'.
[integration] After session.answer(requestId, { decision: "allow" }) on that event, _launcherDeps.runArgv is called with argv [shell, "-c", "curl x"].
[integration] After allowing that event, backend.wrap is not called for the unsandboxed command.
[integration] After session.answer(requestId, { decision: "deny" }) on such an event, neither _launcherDeps.runArgv nor backend.wrap is called.
[integration] After denying that event, the scripted model receives a tool error result.
[integration] A later Bash call { command: "ls" } in the same session, after its own approval is answered allow, calls backend.wrap.

[integration] A full session with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "raw", allowUnsandboxedCommands: true }), probe available and scripted Bash { command: "curl x", unsandboxed: true } emits no approval_requested event.
[integration] That raw session calls _launcherDeps.runArgv with argv [shell, "-c", "curl x"].
[integration] That raw session does not call backend.wrap for the unsandboxed command.
[integration] A full session with nativeBackend({ model, bashApproval: "gated" }) and scripted Bash { command: "curl x", unsandboxed: true } emits no approval_requested event.

userStories.title: Support unsandboxed RunCommand argv requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give RunCommand's Exec argv branch the same opt-in escape argument while refusing it for declared commands.

**Motivation** — The user's rule: "unreachable" (network, Docker socket, local DB port, device) is handled per command, and the sandbox is never turned off for the session.

**Approach** — `RunCommandExecOptions.unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`, forwarded by `buildDeclaredCommandTools` from the same `unsandboxedCommands` arg.

With `exec` set: `scope.unsandboxedField` always; the two schema properties and the argv-worded sentence only when the option is on.

`runExecBranch` passes `unwrapped: true` to `launchExec` and on to the launcher; the declared-command branch rejects the flag with the named error.

`RunCommandExecOptions` / `createRunCommandTool` / `runExecBranch` — Target: `RunCommandExecOptions.unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`. `scope` has `unsandboxedField: "unsandboxed"` whenever `opts.exec` is set. When the option is true and `exec` is set: the same two schema properties and, appended, the sentence `Set "unsandboxed": true with an "unsandboxedReason" only when the argv needs the network, a local socket or a device the sandbox blocks.` `runExecBranch` passes `unwrapped: true` to `launchExec`, which sets it on the `LaunchRequest`. The declared-command (`command`) branch returns `{ content: '"unsandboxed" applies only to "argv" calls', isError: true }` when `input.unsandboxed === true`.

`runExecBranch(input, ctx, opts)` normalizes the argv through the package-manager table (an install such as `["bun","add","x"]` becomes `["bun","add","x","--ignore-scripts"]` when `allowScripts` is false; `["bun","--version"]` is left alone) and forwards `normalized.argv` to the private `launchExec`. Retain that normalization, argv validation, deniedFlag checks, workspace cwd/target, env overlays, signals, result framing and sandbox audit propagation. Check exact true and omit unwrapped for ordinary/non-boolean input; do not let the schema option become a second authorization gate inside the tool.

**Scope** — In: exec option, conditional schema/text and exec-only scope metadata, per-call launch forwarding, declared-command error and support forwarding via the small helper introduced in US-003. Extend run-command-exec-sandbox.test.ts, reusing its existing ["bun","--version"] fixture, and coding-tool-support.test.ts. Out: runtime Exec identity/ask conversion already pinned by US-006, session model scenarios in US-007, or declaring RunCommand for a session profile. RunCommand and Exec are not declared for any session profile in this feature; `declaredToolsFor` is unchanged, so an interactive session does not see RunCommand until a later feature declares it. The RunCommand `unsandboxed` argument is exercised at the tool and support level here.

**Interface** — `RunCommandExecOptions`: `readonly unsandboxedCommands?: boolean`. Exec schema additions: `unsandboxed: { type: "boolean" }`, `unsandboxedReason: { type: "string" }`. Exec scope: `unsandboxedField: "unsandboxed"`. Launcher: `readonly unwrapped?: true`. Declared-command refusal: `{ content: '"unsandboxed" applies only to "argv" calls', isError: true }`. Never add shell execution to run-command-exec.ts or a new public export name.

analysis:
Goal and completion: F1 adds explicit unavailable-sandbox fallback for full/review raw native sessions, immutable sandbox-state reporting at open, and opt-in per-command sandbox escape for Bash and RunCommand argv without weakening policy. Completion requires the eight binding stories, their behavioral assertions and failure cases, and proof that a later ordinary command still wraps after an escaped command. Only packages/nax-agent implementation and tests change; this PRD is the requested planning artifact.

Discovery: codebase-memory MCP is not exposed in this host, so discovery used direct reads and repository text search. The existing feature PRD was read before replacement. Source matches the supplied baseline except that the spec's src/tools/tool-input-validation.ts path does not exist: the actual validator is packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/tool-input-validation.ts:38. Its unknown-property pass-through is at :59-60, optional-null behavior at :64-65, and primitive-type rejection at :67-77. Do not create or move a validator. File paths in contextFiles and expectedFiles are repository-relative; all story workdirs are packages/nax-agent.

Architecture and dependency direction: the package owns session, native runtime, tools, permissions and sandbox. Native options are parsed by a strict zod object while retaining caller identity (packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend-options.ts:62-113). NativeBackendOptions currently declares bashApproval and allowUnsandboxed at :26-27; nativeProfileRules at :128-149 defaults locally to gated, limits the knobs to tool-capable profiles, enforces ask-profile gated before the old allowUnsandboxed/gated restriction, and returns two fields. US-001 adds the third resolved boolean and optional schema field; explicit false still counts as a field being set for none/read. Do not substitute the global raw default for the session/support gated default. nativeBackend validates on construction (:130-138), but openNative resolves profile/sandbox/tool support during open (packages/nax-agent/src/session/native-backend.ts:54-80). This is the production consumer of resolveSessionLauncher; text search also identified its unit tests as consumers.

Sandbox floor and reporting impact: packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-tool-support.ts:28-38 declares existing profile tools; keep that function unchanged, especially no RunCommand/Exec session declaration. askRulesFor at :50-58 adds a Bash ask under gated only, with no Exec ask. resolveSessionLauncher at :89-107 currently returns a bare launcher, skips probing none/read, and drops an unavailable launcher only for gated plus allowUnsandboxed. Change its return atomically with openNative to { launcher, sandbox }, preserve unavailable probe reason, and use disabled only for none/read sessions. The opt-in does not drop an available launcher. BackendInfo at packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-backend.ts:12-17 is the shared native/ACP contract; add optional sandbox, not a required field for ACP. openNative currently returns two-field info at native-backend.ts:117. FacadeAgentSession.backend at packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session.ts:73-76 reconstructs info and freezes capabilities; it must copy and shallow-freeze a fresh sandbox object when present, omit the key when absent, and keep existing freezing. Reporting is a construction-time snapshot, not a per-command toggle or probe loop.

Launcher impact: SandboxState, SandboxRecord and LaunchRequest are at packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/types.ts:70, :85 and :102. createCommandLauncher at packages/nax-agent/src/sandbox/launcher.ts:182-223 owns one immutable state and recreates its temp directory before each run. Insert requested-unwrapped routing after that temp setup and before disabled/unavailable/available routing. runUnwrapped at :109-121 already computes logical shell/argv execution and caller env handling; withTmpEnv at :81-84 gives request env precedence over TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP defaults. Reuse it rather than adding a spawn mechanism. An explicit request must record { backend: none, wrapped: false, reason: requested } for every launcher state, skip policyFor and afterWrapped, and leave the launcher's state unchanged. Ordinary unavailable/disabled records and available wrap-failure fail-closed behavior remain unchanged. runWrapped at :123-180 retains logical executed argv, wrapper bookkeeping and denial annotations. _launcherDeps.runArgv is the safe spawn seam.

Tool/support wiring: buildSessionToolSupport at packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-tool-support.ts:127-150 creates grants, ask rules and support without auditDir. buildCodingToolSupport at packages/nax-agent/src/coding-tools/coding-tool-support.ts:69-310 resolves bashApproval at :186, compiles policy at :248-258, creates the runtime at :247, and delegates command tools at :283. supportSink at :332-346 is no-op without auditDir; do not add session audit storage. buildDeclaredCommandTools at packages/nax-agent/src/coding-tools/coding-tool-extras.ts:43-97 constructs RunCommand and Bash, including exec options and launcher propagation. US-003 threads unsandboxedCommands through openNative and these layers to Bash; US-005 wires the runtime option using the locally resolved mode; US-008 completes exec-option plumbing. Use a small extracted helper in each support builder so existing complexity does not grow. ToolScope at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/types.ts:76-133 gets an optional metadata field, not a new policy permission. Bash must always expose scope.unsandboxedField even when its public schema omits the flag; runtime enforcement must catch hallucinated extra input. createBashTool at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/bash.ts:311-386 has the baseline schema at :321-332 and command scope at :336. launchIntercepted at :261-309 preserves interception/revalidation, overlays and direct spawn; add a per-call flag through its request and conditionally include unwrapped only for exact true. The tool does not enforce session enablement; that belongs to the runtime. Off/absent schemas and descriptions are byte-identical, including platform and sandbox description endings.

Approval flow: AskRequest at packages/nax-agent/src/permissions/types.ts:13-45 distinguishes matchedRule origin from a display rule. resolveAskOutcome at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts:212-281 currently sets matchedRule for every defined verdict.rule (:239) and reason verbatim (:248); preserve real-rule origins but exclude synthetic Unsandboxed(Bash/Exec) origins. Add optional suffix metadata, not a new ask kind. Existing abort-after-allow recheck at :270-277 must remain. askSummary at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/ask-request.ts:39-53 masks the full string before slicing to MAX_ASK_SUMMARY_CHARS (200); mirror that ordering for the new reason renderer, using no reason given for non-string/missing and reason withheld for unsafe masking. Do not make the reason schema-required: missing reasons still ask with the specified fallback. The approval chain is AskRequest -> createSessionAskLink (packages/nax-agent/src/session/session-ask-link.ts:63-83) -> ApprovalRequest (session-backend.ts:19-27) -> createSessionAskPort.requestApproval (session-ask-port.ts:33-39, strips signal using rest-spread) -> ApprovalAsk (session-ask-link.ts:24-30) -> askPerson event (:39-49) -> session.answer. Add optional literal true throughout, including the approval_requested union in agent-session-types.ts:105-116, and omit absent keys to preserve old event shapes. ACP translation is not modified.

Runtime security boundary: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime.ts:153 defines runtime options; callTool at :359 resolves lookup, derives identity at :367 and calls policy.check at :369. resolvePolicyIdentity at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/runtime-calltool.ts:89-94 switches a RunCommand argv call to Exec but leaves declared-command calls as RunCommand. resolveUnsandboxedCall belongs in runtime-calltool.ts and must be invoked before policy.check, once per call; identity must be Bash/Exec, scope must declare the field, and only exact true activates routing. Disabled/missing enablement produces the exact error and audit outcome before any policy/ask/spawn. This introduces an early result before the current logCall wrapper, which is declared after policy and shadow setup (runtime.ts:390-419); arrange the helper/callback seam so early refusal is recorded through the same logging semantics without evaluating policy first or opening a shadow tap unnecessarily. Keep callTool compact; do not inline the routing matrix. Enabled calls compute the ordinary policy verdict without the escape flag influencing permissions, but retain the original input for the tool and audit. Existing ask branch at :502-518 and denial branch at :521-536 stay fail-closed. Denials preserve existing redirect/breach semantics via resolveDenialOutcome (runtime-calltool.ts:286-330). Non-raw allows convert to an ask with preserved resolvedPaths, reason unsandboxed run requested, synthetic rule and no matchedRule. Real asks gain suffix/flag; raw allows run with no new approval event. The guard-denial ask at runtime.ts:550 is deliberately not decorated. US-005 handles enablement/denial/ordinary-call invariants and human refusal; US-006 completes converted asks and raw/direct-spawn routing, extending the same helper and test file rather than inventing another subsystem.

RunCommand impact: RunCommandExecOptions is at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/run-command.ts:36-56; createRunCommandTool at :337 builds an exec-dependent schema and scope (:355-403), and run at :405 first enforces exclusive command/argv shape. Add exec-only scope metadata and option-gated schema/text, and reject exact true on the declared branch before invoking its runner. Mirror the existing target-only-on-argv refusal near :415. runExecBranch at packages/nax-agent/src/tools/run-command-exec.ts:109-186 rechecks argv and redirecting flags, normalizes installs/workspace target at :133-142 and passes normalized.argv to launchExec at :153-162. Forward the new flag without bypassing any hardening or importing the shell-templated declared runner. For bun --version argv remains unchanged; bun add still receives --ignore-scripts when scripts are disabled. launchExec at :74-106 needs a conditional unwrapped property while preserving cwd, timeout, env and signal.

outOfScope: RunCommand and Exec are not declared for any session profile in this feature; `declaredToolsFor` is unchanged, so an interactive session does not see RunCommand until a later feature declares it. The RunCommand `unsandboxed` argument is exercised at the tool and support level here.

No tool-audit directory is plumbed into sessions; `buildSessionToolSupport` keeps the non-recording sink, so an unsandboxed run under `raw` leaves no durable session ledger row. Callers that pass `auditDir` to `buildCodingToolSupport` get the `reason: "requested"` record.
No approvals-cache link is added to the session ask chain; a `gated` session asks the human for every Bash command, as today.
No mutable profile or `bashApproval` on an open session; switching mode is the host's job (close and reopen on the same transcript).

The ACP server (`packages/nax-agent-acp`) does not expose `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxed` with `raw`, `BackendInfo.sandbox` or the `unsandboxed` approval field; its config and translate layers are unchanged.
`packages/nax` is unchanged: no nax config key, no `nax run` wiring, no CLI flag for the new options, and the Telegram and other interaction channels do not render `unsandboxed`.
`AskDecidedBy` gains no new value, and no approval event is emitted under `raw`.
The guard-denial ask path (`commandShadow.guard` in `callTool`) does not carry the `unsandboxed` flag; sessions configure no command shadow, so it is inert here.
`escalate` mode semantics are unchanged; `allowUnsandboxed` with `escalate` stays invalid.
The `.nax` protected-path refusals, the Claude settings file refusals and the raw-mode lexical screen (`screenRawBashCommand`) are unchanged.
`unsandboxed: true` does not bypass policy evaluation: deny rules, payload checks, containment, the lexer and grant evaluation run exactly as without the flag.
Launcher-level relaxations that read the session's sandbox state (`rawScreenOptionsFor`, `isTempConfined`) are not re-decided per call; they are inert in sessions and unchanged for nax run callers.
Remembered-approval keys in `packages/nax` do not include the `unsandboxed` flag; whether a remembered plain approval should cover an unsandboxed variant is a later decision.
`SandboxState` is reported once at open; a sandbox that becomes unavailable mid-session is not re-probed.

Sessions always use `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_CONFIG` (enabled), so the `disabled` sandbox state arises only for the `none` and `read` profiles; a config-disabled sandbox combined with `allowUnsandboxed` is not a session case.
No per-command unsandboxed path for `Write`, `Edit`, `Delete`, `Git` or `GitCommit`; those tools do not run through the launcher.
Session storage sharing with the ACP server (feature F2), the terminal UI (F3), the skills and plugin loader (F4) and MCP servers and subagents (F5) are separate features.
No dependency bumps; `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` stays at its current version.
